angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 340,893 km at 75.49 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.2466 +/- 0.0176 mas (same row, RUWE 1.01): 75.49 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.49 +/- 0.01 solar radii from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-344 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract): 340,893 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.51 +/- 0.01 solar masses from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-344 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4374 +/- 38 K from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-344 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-344 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-344.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.765, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
